paragraphs.en: How our readers help us fight for a shared reality
paragraphs.zh: 读者如何助力我们守护共同的真实世界

paragraphs.en: It is because we have put human-centred, hopeful, public-interest journalism first that we have built such a loyal community of readers.
paragraphs.zh: 正是因为我们始终把以人为本、饱含希望、服务公共利益的新闻报道放在首位，才凝聚起如此忠实的读者社群。

paragraphs.en: And it is those readers who sustain our work.
paragraphs.zh: 而支撑我们开展一切工作的，正是这些读者。

paragraphs.en: When I became editor in 2015, the Guardian had been loss-making for a long time, and, although the Scott Trust sustained the losses, we were depleted and vulnerable.
paragraphs.zh: 2015年我就任主编时，《卫报》长期处于亏损状态，尽管斯科特信托基金会持续承担亏损，报社资源已然枯竭，处境岌岌可危。

paragraphs.en: We had no effective business model, no digital reader revenue.
paragraphs.zh: 彼时我们没有成熟的商业模式，也没有来自数字端读者的收入。

paragraphs.en: But today the Guardian's model is admired across the world.
paragraphs.zh: 但如今，《卫报》的运营模式得到全球同行的认可。

paragraphs.en: We made a lot of very tough decisions to get to this position.
paragraphs.zh: 为走到今天这一步，我们做出了诸多艰难抉择。

paragraphs.en: But the one that had the biggest impact was introducing voluntary financial contributions – the idea that our readers choose to give us money for something they could get for free.
paragraphs.zh: 其中影响最为深远的举措，便是推出自愿捐助机制——即读者可以自愿付费，获取本可免费阅读的内容。

paragraphs.en: When we launched it, in 2016, we were pretty desperate.
paragraphs.zh: 2016年推出该机制时，我们已然走投无路。

paragraphs.en: There was huge pressure to put up a paywall, which would have meant that only people with money could access the Guardian.
paragraphs.zh: 当时外界强烈要求我们设置付费墙，一旦落地，只有付费人群才能阅读《卫报》。

paragraphs.en: It would have blunted our impact. It would have reduced our civic role.
paragraphs.zh: 这会削弱我们的传播影响力，弱化我们的公共服务职能。

paragraphs.en: So instead, against most advice, we asked our audience to give us money, rather than forcing them to.
paragraphs.zh: 于是我们顶住多数人的反对意见，没有强制收费，而是向读者发起自愿捐助的倡议。

paragraphs.en: And they did. They understood right away what we were trying to do.
paragraphs.zh: 而读者们伸出了援手。他们立刻读懂了我们的初衷。

paragraphs.en: In the last financial year, our readers directly gave us more than ￡125m.
paragraphs.zh: 上一财年，读者向我们自愿捐助总额超过1.25亿英镑。

paragraphs.en: We have people who give us money from everywhere on the planet, right down to some of the smallest countries and most sparsely populated places on Earth: yes, we have readers making financial contributions to the Guardian from Nauru and Svalbard and Vatican City and Antarctica.
paragraphs.zh: 全球各地都有捐助者，即便是地球上国土面积极小、人口极度稀疏的地区也不例外：瑙鲁、斯瓦尔巴群岛、梵蒂冈，甚至南极，都有读者为《卫报》捐款。

paragraphs.en: It shouldn't work, but it does, and in this moment, in particular, it's inspiring and important that it does.
paragraphs.zh: 这套模式本看似行不通，却实实在在运转起来，尤其在当下这个时代，这份支撑既鼓舞人心，也意义重大。

paragraphs.en: Almost 1.5 million people give us money every month, and that number is increasing every day.
paragraphs.zh: 每月有近150万人持续定期捐助，且这个数字每日都在增长。

paragraphs.en: Many more give us one-off contributions for an article they liked.
paragraphs.zh: 还有更多读者会为一篇心仪的报道一次性捐款。

paragraphs.en: As our supporters have often told us, many of them are giving us money so that other people can read the Guardian for free, and to be part of something that really matters.
paragraphs.zh: 许多捐助者和我们说，他们捐款，是为了让其他人能够免费阅读《卫报》，参与一件真正有价值的事业。

paragraphs.en: Some also tell us that they see our successful attempts to keep good information available to all as a highly political act.
paragraphs.zh: 也有读者表示，我们坚持向所有人开放优质资讯的努力，本身就是极具政治意义的行动。

paragraphs.en: We value our readers' support not just for their money, but for their ideas, their community and their belief that we don't have to accept things as they are, that we can, together, make the world a better place.
paragraphs.zh: 我们珍视读者的支持，不只因为捐助资金，更看重他们带来的观点、构筑的社群，以及他们共同秉持的信念：我们不必被动接受当下的现状，众人携手，便能让世界变得更好。

paragraphs.en: Indeed, it is only by acting together, as a community, that we can hope to save our beautiful planet from climate breakdown.
paragraphs.zh: 事实上，唯有社群同心协力，我们才有希望守护美丽的地球，避免气候崩溃。

paragraphs.en: Step back, and it forms a virtuous circle.
paragraphs.zh: 放眼全局，这形成了良性循环。

paragraphs.en: Our ownership model enables us to make our public-interest journalism available to all, and invite voluntary contributions from our audience to support our work.
paragraphs.zh: 独特的所有制模式让我们能够向所有人开放公共新闻，并向读者发起自愿捐助以维系采编工作。

paragraphs.en: And because our audience are not forced to pay, they do not feel like consumers, or as commodities monetised for clicks, but as members of a community.
paragraphs.zh: 读者无需被迫付费，因此他们不会觉得自己只是消费者，或是被流量变现的商品，而是社群的一份子。

paragraphs.en: The Guardian helps to equip this community with facts and ideas to understand the world and to engage in it, and this community likewise helps the Guardian to continue to deliver meaningful journalism.
paragraphs.zh: 《卫报》为社群提供事实与观点，帮助大家理解世界、参与公共事务；而这份社群力量，反过来支撑《卫报》持续产出有价值的报道。

paragraphs.en: Journalism is not a "content business".
paragraphs.zh: 新闻行业绝非一门“内容生意”。

paragraphs.en: Let no one use that term when talking about public-interest journalism!
paragraphs.zh: 谈及公共新闻事业，绝不该使用这个说法！

paragraphs.en: No, it is a part of our shared civic infrastructure, human infrastructure, societal infrastructure.
paragraphs.zh: 新闻是全民共有的公共基础设施、人文基础设施、社会基础设施的一环。

paragraphs.en: It's the connective tissue that helps fight isolation and sustains democracy.
paragraphs.zh: 它如同联结社会的纽带，消解人与人的隔绝，维系民主制度。

paragraphs.en: Part of its role, to quote Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor, should be to counter the "apocalyptic narratives with a far better story about how to survive the hard times ahead without leaving anyone behind".
paragraphs.zh: 引用娜奥米·克莱因与阿斯特拉·泰勒的观点，新闻的使命之一，是抗衡各类末日论调，讲述一个更美好的故事：我们该如何共度未来的艰难岁月，不抛下任何一个人。

paragraphs.en: In 2017, when I first laid out my interpretation of the Guardian's history in the contemporary context, I argued that facts and ideas, together, make the space for hope.
paragraphs.zh: 2017年，我首次结合当下时代背景阐释《卫报》的发展脉络，当时我提出：事实与思想相结合，方能孕育希望的空间。

paragraphs.en: By hope, I do not mean blind optimism that everything will work out OK.
paragraphs.zh: 我所说的希望，并非盲目乐观，认定万事都会迎刃而解。

paragraphs.en: Hope is about having faith that we have the power and agency to change the future.
paragraphs.zh: 希望，是坚信我们拥有改变未来的力量与主动权。

paragraphs.en: Connecting with each other – just as I did when I finally found a way to write this article – is a good place to start.
paragraphs.zh: 人与人彼此联结——就像我最终理清思路写完这篇文章时所体会到的那样——便是迈出改变的第一步。

paragraphs.en: To fight for the Guardian and organisations like it is not just fighting for a business model; it's fighting for the human right to live in a reality that is shared and true and that we can each help to shape.
paragraphs.zh: 捍卫《卫报》以及同类公共新闻机构，不只是捍卫一种商业模式；更是捍卫一项人权：生活在真实、共通、人人都能参与塑造的现实之中。

paragraphs.en: It is urgent: the world won't wait. Hope and connection are how we survive, together.
paragraphs.zh: 形势迫在眉睫，世界不会原地等待。希望与联结，是我们共存共生的出路。

paragraphs.en: How we stay human. We are not alone. There are many millions of us.
paragraphs.zh: 是我们守住人性的根基。我们从不孤单。千千万万的人与我们同行。
